title: Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda
snippet: The case was identified following the clinical deterioration and death of an adult male patient from the DRC who was admitted to a private hospital in Kampala, Uganda, in May 2026. Demographic information, including patient sex and travel history from the DRC, was extracted from a standardized national VHF case investigation form and the electronic case admission record. Given the clinical course, an incomplete epidemiological history and regional concern for VHF, a posthumous EDTA whole-blood [...] no blood work was performed before he left, and then self-referred to a private hospital in Kampala. On admission on 11 May 2026, the patient presented with severe vomiting, frequent diarrhea, intermittent epigastric pain, generalized weakness and hiccups; vomiting and diarrhea had reportedly persisted for more than 2 weeks, although the exact symptom onset date was not ascertained. Add NBC News to Google [...] By Jane Weaver, Jiachuan Wu and Javier Zarracina

The ongoing Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has alarmed global public health experts for the ferocity of the spread in the remote and heavily populated region. Since the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency in mid-May, there have been hundreds of confirmed cases and dozens of deaths from the Bundibugyo species of the virus. [...] There’s no vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo virus, although there are two potential vaccine candidates, according to the WHO. Neither is ready for testing on humans.

There are four species of the Ebola virus that are known to cause disease in humans, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
